reuse.why: The new range consumer and existing consumers reuse getDateWithSkippedWeekend, while recurrence generation continues through recurConfigToRSchedule and RSchedule.

duplication.why: Holiday matching and date adjustment are shared, although the skipWeekend dispatch and adjustment argument assembly remain repeated across consumers.

placement.why: Calendar policy remains in shared/schedules.ts, configuration metadata flows through rule parsing, and the new handler follows the existing schedule server layer.

scope.why: The changes are focused on the requested scheduling rules, range handler, supporting configuration, tests, and release note.

maintainability.why: Centralized holiday matching and adjustment make future rule changes straightforward, though loosely typed configuration and repeated positional argument assembly weaken the interface.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changed date-adjustment consumers call the existing shared getDateWithSkippedWeekend abstraction.

disguised_duplication.where: The repeated adjustment dispatch is explicit; holiday matching and movement logic are shared rather than disguised.

abstraction_drift.where: getDateWithSkippedWeekend adds frequency and holidays parameters and a daily-frequency branch returning null; all changed consumers continue using it.
